interactions.label: Guided focus
interactions.teaches: The learner separates the whole-network dataflow from the local residual-block mechanism, then sees how the two levels of detail fit together.
Clicking a residual stage shows that the same bottleneck ResBlock pattern is reused at each spatial scale while the visible tensor dimensions remain fixed by the architecture.

interactions.label: Animate ResBlock forward pass
interactions.teaches: The learner sees the transformed path and the identity skip path arrive at the addition node together, making the residual output a sum rather than a replacement.

demo_steps.title: Whole ResNet flow
demo_steps.narration: The image enters at 224×224×3, passes through the 7×7 convolution and MaxPool, then flows left-to-right through four residual stages before AvgPool, FC, and Softmax.

demo_steps.title: Spatial size shrinks while depth grows
demo_steps.narration: The Subsample transitions reduce feature-map size from 56 to 28 to 14 to 7, while the channel count grows from 256 to 512 to 1024 to 2048. The cuboids become shorter but longer, matching the labels.

demo_steps.title: Repeated residual stages
demo_steps.narration: The ellipses and fixed annotations such as '24 blocks total' and '36 blocks total' indicate repeated ResBlocks in the source architecture. They are not an adjustable depth control; they are part of the depicted network.

demo_steps.title: Inside one ResBlock
demo_steps.narration: The upper inset expands a single ResBlock: Conv 1×1, BN, ReLU, Conv 3×3, BN, ReLU, Conv 1×1. The skip connection carries the input around these layers to the addition node.

plan.geometry_notes: Use a wide oblique layout with +X screen-right following network flow, +Y screen-up, and +Z as the receding diagonal slanting up-right. Overall world extents about X=-8.8 to +8.4, Y=-2.0 to +3.6, Z=0 to 1.0. Keep the main architecture in the lower half, centered near Y=-0.55, and the ResBlock inset large across the upper portion, centered near Y=2.55. Input image: front rectangle at X≈-8.1, Y≈-0.45, size X×Y×Z ≈ 1.05×1.55×0.10, with its visible front face a dark warm photo-like texture: nearly black background #080604, dark brown #2a1207, orange vertical glow #d47417, small yellow-white highlight #ffe36a. Add a dark side slab #111111 offset along +Z on the right/back edge, visibly thicker than the image plane, so the panel resembles the source image with a black receding side. The first orange convolution tensor is at X≈-6.65, size 0.18×1.05×0.36, color #bd7650 with darker edges #6d3b25. For tensor boxes, encode channel depth mostly as X length, spatial height as Y, and spatial width as Z; all dimensions are schematic but must preserve relative trends. 56×56×256 stage: show three short blue blocks from X≈-5.85 to -4.55, each about 0.52×0.62×0.34, color #a9c4d1 with edge #2f5667. 28×28×512 stage: place from X≈-3.35 to -1.65; visible blocks about 0.90×0.36×0.25, longer than the 56 stage blocks but clearly shorter in height; include ellipsis between first and last block. 14×14×1024 stage: place from X≈-0.75 to +1.45; blocks about 1.45×0.22×0.18, low and elongated. 7×7×2048 stage: place from X≈+2.55 to +5.95; blocks about 2.35×0.13×0.12, very long and thin; keep enough spacing so it does not collide with the classifier. Classifier bars at X≈+6.9 and +7.25, each about 0.16×1.1×0.12, teal #7fc6c0, with dark zigzag breaks. Labels should match the source labels only: tensor dimensions, ResBlock, Subsample, fixed '24 blocks total', fixed '36 blocks total', AvgPool + FC, 1000, Softmax. Do not add an active-depth label, adjustable-depth label, or extra inset channel sublabels. The top inset rounded rectangle should span about X=-6.9 to +7.55 and Y=1.75 to 3.35, fill #cfd6d8, outline #222222. Inset input cube at X≈-6.35, Y≈2.50, size 0.38×0.38×0.20, blue #a9c4d1. Operation boxes along a horizontal main path at Y≈2.38: Conv boxes gray #d7dedf, BN boxes orange #d18459, ReLU boxes teal #90cfc7; each about 0.82×0.42, spaced evenly from X≈-4.9 to +4.2. Skip line runs above the boxes at Y≈3.05 from near the input branch to the circled plus at X≈+5.55, then drops down into the addition node. Addition node is a white circle with black outline and '⊕', radius about 0.18. Output arrow extends to X≈+6.45.
plan.notes: Render with an orthographic oblique-style projection or apply a consistent shear so front faces remain rectangular and depth recedes diagonally. The guidedFocus state should only dim, highlight, or lightly outline existing source elements; it must not introduce new architecture choices or change fixed block-count annotations. selectStage should highlight the clicked residual stage and optionally draw a thin connector to the inset, but keep the inset labels generic as in the source rather than adding stage-specific channel sublabels. The ResBlock animation should use two colored pulses: a blue pulse through the Conv/BN/ReLU main path and a gold pulse along the skip path; both meet at the circled plus, which briefly glows before the output arrow lights. Use CSS2D or high-resolution canvas sprites for labels so the dense text remains legible in the PDF embedding.

authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates the architecture of a deep residual network (ResNet) at two levels of detail. The main diagram traces the flow of feature tensors through successive stages of the network, with labeled spatial and channel dimensions at each stage: a 7x7 convolution produces 112x112x64 feature maps, which are then processed through four residual stages yielding progressively smaller but deeper tensors — 56x56x256, 28x28x512, 14x14x1024, and 7x7x2048 — before a final average pooling and fully connected (AvgPool + FC) layer. Between stages, Subsample blocks reduce spatial resolution while increasing channel depth; within each stage, repeated ResBlocks (indicated by ellipses and annotations such as '24 blocks total' and '36 blocks total') apply the same transformation many times. An inset zooms into the internal structure of a single ResBlock, showing the sequence: Conv 1x1 (bottleneck squeeze), Batch Normalization (BN), ReLU, Conv 3x3 (spatial convolution), BN, ReLU, and Conv 1x1 (channel expansion), with a skip connection bypassing these layers and adding the input directly to the output. The figure introduces the residual (skip-connection) design that allows very deep networks to be trained effectively by ensuring gradients can flow directly from later to earlier layers.
authoredInteractions:
- Animate the residual block forward pass: trace the signal through the main path and simultaneously along the parallel 1×1 skip connection, then show the element-wise addition (⊕) combining both paths at the block output
- Slider for ResNet depth (24 blocks / 36 blocks): update the number of residual blocks shown per stage and the total block-count label, while the tensor dimensions at each stage (112×112×64 through 7×7×2048) remain constant
- Click on a stage's tensor block: zoom in to display the bottleneck detail with Conv 1×1 channel compression, Conv 3×3 spatial processing, and Conv 1×1 expansion, with the specific channel counts (e.g., 64 bottleneck, 256 output) labeled for that stage

For stageZoom clicks, keep the top inset in place but update its labels to show the selected stage's spatial size, bottleneck channels, and expansion channels; optionally dim nonselected stages and add a thin connector line from the clicked tensor to the inset.

discrepancies: The large brown MaxPool/output slab after the initial convolution in the source is effectively missing; only a thin orange tensor is shown before the blue residual-stage blocks.
The main architecture is much more compressed and low in height than the source, making the staged tensors and long 7×7 blocks appear flattened and less visually prominent.
Many source labels are angled along arrows and brackets, while the generated labels are horizontal and crowded around the tensors, reducing resemblance and readability.
The generated figure changes the original fixed '24 blocks total' and '36 blocks total' annotations into an interactive depth/repeats display, so the default labels do not match the source exactly.
An extra dashed connector and 'ResBlock detail' explanatory label link the main network to the inset, which is not present in the original figure.
The inset ResBlock is structurally similar but scaled and positioned smaller relative to the full figure than in the source, and includes extra channel-number details inside Conv labels.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure captures the ResNet pipeline and bottleneck inset well, but missing/altered early-stage geometry, crowded labels, scale compression, and extra explanatory elements reduce fidelity to the source.
action_items: Add the prominent brown MaxPool/output slab after the initial convolution so the left side matches the source architecture.
Increase the figure scale and spacing, especially between early residual stages, to reduce label crowding and better match the wide textbook layout.
Rotate and place dimension, ResBlock, Subsample, AvgPool/FC, and Softmax labels along their corresponding arrows/brackets as in the source.
Restore the default fixed annotations '24 blocks total' and '36 blocks total' in the same positions as the source, using the slider only as an optional overlay or alternate mode.
plan_action_items: Revise the plan so interactive depth changes do not replace source annotations that should be simultaneously visible in the static architecture figure.

feedback.rationale: The ResNet concept and interactivity are largely correct, while the main problems are implementation-level fidelity issues—missing slab, scale/spacing, label placement, and extra explanatory elements—with only a minor interaction annotation adjustment needed.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates the architecture of a deep residual network (ResNet) at two levels of detail. The main diagram traces the flow of feature tensors through successive stages of the network, with labeled spatial and channel dimensions at each stage: a 7x7 convolution produces 112x112x64 feature maps, which are then processed through four residual stages yielding progressively smaller but deeper tensors — 56x56x256, 28x28x512, 14x14x1024, and 7x7x2048 — before a final average pooling and fully connected (AvgPool + FC) layer. Between stages, Subsample blocks reduce spatial resolution while increasing channel depth; within each stage, repeated ResBlocks (indicated by ellipses and annotations such as '24 blocks total' and '36 blocks total') apply the same transformation many times. An inset zooms into the internal structure of a single ResBlock, showing the sequence: Conv 1x1 (bottleneck squeeze), Batch Normalization (BN), ReLU, Conv 3x3 (spatial convolution), BN, ReLU, and Conv 1x1 (channel expansion), with a skip connection bypassing these layers and adding the input directly to the output. The figure introduces the residual (skip-connection) design that allows very deep networks to be trained effectively by ensuring gradients can flow directly from later to earlier layers.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Animate the residual block forward pass: trace the signal through the main path and simultaneously along the parallel 1×1 skip connection, then show the element-wise addition (⊕) combining both paths at the block output
- Slider for ResNet depth (24 blocks / 36 blocks): update the number of residual blocks shown per stage and the total block-count label, while the tensor dimensions at each stage (112×112×64 through 7×7×2048) remain constant
- Click on a stage's tensor block: zoom in to display the bottleneck detail with Conv 1×1 channel compression, Conv 3×3 spatial processing, and Conv 1×1 expansion, with the specific channel counts (e.g., 64 bottleneck, 256 output) labeled for that stage

interactions.label: Guided focus
interactions.teaches: The learner separates the whole-network dataflow from the local residual-block mechanism, then sees how the two levels of detail fit together.
Clicking a residual stage shows that the same bottleneck ResBlock pattern is reused at each spatial scale while the visible tensor dimensions remain fixed by the architecture.

interactions.label: Animate ResBlock forward pass
interactions.teaches: The learner sees the transformed path and the identity skip path arrive at the addition node together, making the residual output a sum rather than a replacement.

demo_steps.title: Whole ResNet flow
demo_steps.narration: The image enters at 224×224×3, passes through the 7×7 convolution and MaxPool, then flows left-to-right through four residual stages before AvgPool, FC, and Softmax.

demo_steps.title: Spatial size shrinks while depth grows
demo_steps.narration: The Subsample transitions reduce feature-map size from 56 to 28 to 14 to 7, while the channel count grows from 256 to 512 to 1024 to 2048. The cuboids become shorter but longer, matching the labels.

demo_steps.title: Repeated residual stages
demo_steps.narration: The ellipses and fixed annotations such as '24 blocks total' and '36 blocks total' indicate repeated ResBlocks in the source architecture. They are not an adjustable depth control; they are part of the depicted network.

demo_steps.title: Inside one ResBlock
demo_steps.narration: The upper inset expands a single ResBlock: Conv 1×1, BN, ReLU, Conv 3×3, BN, ReLU, Conv 1×1. The skip connection carries the input around these layers to the addition node.
